answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making trust something earned over time, not minted on demand: a new identity starts with zero standing and must complete small, verifiable jobs checked by independent peers, like a ship proving itself across an ocean before the far horizon comes into view. Influence grows only as a record of honest work accumulates, so spawning thousands of fake identities buys nothing - each one must separately climb from nothing toward its zenith, and faking that history costs more than one extra vote is worth.
